restoration_note: The teaching describes the daily round of sun and night as the two visible mysteries (the sun = Jesus the Radiance/Divine Truth manifesting the unburied Father of Greatness; the night = the shadow of the King of Darkness). Restorations are heavily constrained by (1) the kephalaion's enumerative formulae (ⲡⲛⲉⲩ ⲉⲧⲉⲣⲉ + subject; ⲡⲁⲣⲁ + comparator), (2) standard Manichaean dyad 'mystery of the light / mystery of the darkness', (3) Lycopolitan word-breaks across line ends (ⲣ-ⲫⲟ-ⲣⲉ; ⲡⲓⲙⲟⲩ-ⲍ; ⲙ̄ⲙⲏ-ⲛⲉ), and (4) preserved partial traces. All sixteen gaps could be restored with at least moderate confidence; gap {4} (ⲛⲁⲟⲩⲣⲡ̄ϣⲉ) remains lexically uncertain but its Coptic is physically present, so only the English equivalent is tentative.

restorations.basis: Word ⲣⲫⲟⲣⲉ (Greek φορεῖν) is split across line break: ⲣ{0} + ⲣⲉ on next line. Editor's ⲫⲟ completes the verb 'bear/come upon'. Lexicon: ⲣ̄ⲫⲟⲣⲉ = 'clothe / put truth into external form / wear'; here in transferred sense the night's shadow 'bears upon' all men.

ⲙⲟⲩ{1} completed as ⲙⲟⲩϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('be filled forth'); next line ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩϣⲏ supplies the agent ('by the night'), forming the standard ⲙⲟⲩϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲛ̄- construction. Spiritually: the cosmos is wholly filled with the falsity-from-evil of the night.

Each numbered evil/good in this kephalaion is introduced by ⲡⲛⲉⲩ ⲉⲧⲉⲣⲉ + subject (cf. lines 75, 82, 85: ⲡⲛⲉⲩ ⲉⲧⲉⲣⲉ ⲧⲉⲥϩⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ / ⲡⲛⲉⲩ ⲉⲧϩⲁⲡⲣⲓⲉ / ⲡⲛⲉⲩ ⲁⲛ ⲉⲧⲉⲣⲉ ⲡⲣⲏ). The third item under the night requires the same formula with ⲧⲟⲩϣⲏ as subject.

Qualitative ⲛⲉⲥⲉ- (be beautiful) closing the comparative pattern 'ⲡⲉϩⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ ⲧⲣⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ ... ⲡⲁⲣⲁ ⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ' / 'ⲡⲉϩⲥⲁⲓⲉ ⲁⲛ ⲛⲉⲥⲉ ⲡⲁⲣⲁ ⲛⲥⲁⲓⲉ ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ'. Each of the five sun-works gets a 'beyond all X' coda; here the verb of beauty is needed.

Coptic is physically preserved (ⲛⲁⲟⲩⲣⲡ̄ϣⲉ); only the English equivalent is uncertain. Following the editor's tentative reading, the term parallels ⲛ̄ⲟ̄ⲁⲙ ('powers') in the comparative series 'beyond all powers and rulers in the cosmos' — i.e., the cosmic principalities of the natural heavens.

Editor restores final ⲍ to give ⲡⲓⲙⲟⲩⲍ (= ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill, fullness'). Confirmed by the immediately following relative clause ⲉⲧϥⲙⲏⲍ ⲛⲍⲏⲧϥ ('when it is filled in him'). Spiritually: the moon's measured fullness contrasted with the sun's undiminishing disc.
Standard kephalaion formula ⲍⲏ̄ ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ ('in the cosmos'), recurrent throughout this teaching (cf. lines 81, 93, 123). The preceding ⲡ supplies the masculine article.

Preserved ⲡⲉϩⲟ at line end + ⲁⲧⲃⲉ ('exalted') at start of next line require ⲡⲉϩⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲃⲉ ('his light is exalted'). Parallel to lines 93, 109. The second 'type' is the supereminent light of the sun corresponding to the light of the Father.

Preserved ⲛⲉϩⲁ- + Lycopolitan epenthetic ϩ gives ⲛⲉϩⲁⲓⲱⲛ. The sun's light is exalted beyond the light of the aeons (heavenly states), corresponding to the mystery of the Father's light beyond every emanated state. Lexicon: ⲁⲓⲱⲛ = 'a state of divine love and wisdom / heavenly community'.
Standard pairing ⲛ̄ⲥⲏⲩ ⲛⲓⲙ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ ⲛⲓⲙ ('at every season and at every hour'), with ⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ ⲛⲓⲙ preserved on next line. Indicates the Father's eternal hiddenness in his icon ϣⲁ ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ.

Standard demonstrative interjection opening the second mystery section. Mirrors line 134 ⲉⲓⲥ ⲡⲙⲩⲥⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ within the same passage. Short fill consistent with apparatus note that only ⲥ is visible at line start.

Verb ⲉⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('come forth') split across line break: ⲛⲉⲧⲟⲩⲉ-ⲓ + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ on next line. The visible ⲛⲉⲧⲟⲩⲉ is the relative-circumstantial preformative; the gap completes the verb-stem ⲉⲓ before the preserved ⲁⲃⲁⲗ.

Previous line ends ⲙⲡⲟⲩ-, next visible begins ⲙⲛ̄ ⲡⲙⲩⲥⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ ⲙⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ. The standard Manichaean dyad 'mystery of the light / mystery of the darkness' supplies ⲡⲙⲩⲥⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ; the gap restores -ⲁⲓⲛⲉ continuing ⲙⲡⲟⲩ-.
Word ⲙ̄ⲙⲏⲛⲉ ('daily') split across line break: ⲙ̄ⲙⲏ at end of preceding line + ⲛⲉ at start of this line. Completes the recurrent formula ⲥⲉⲟⲩⲁⲛⲍ̄ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲙ̄ⲙⲏⲛⲉ 'they are revealed daily'.

Editor's restoration ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲟⲩⲡⲗⲁⲛⲏ ('in their wandering / circuit') confirmed by the parallel earlier in the kephalaion. Here used in the astronomical sense — the daily circuit of the luminaries — through which the visible mysteries become legible. Not the negative cosmic Error but the wandering-motion as ordered sign.

Final -ⲙⲉⲓ̈ⲛⲉ preserved; restored definite-plural ⲛⲙ̄- (Lyc. ⲛ̄-). Construction: 'to reveal all the signs of his graces'. The sun, as Divine Truth in its illuminating manifestation, makes visible (ⲟⲩⲁⲛⲍ̄ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ) the signs (ⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ) of the Father's gifts.
